thread:
Iris: New hire here trying the hosted quickstart with SSO-linked workspace. I created a personal API key via the SDK page but my first /v1/chat returns 402. Dashboard shows workspace active and a card on file. anyone know SSO/key scoping gotchas? :confused:

Jam: do you mean you used the 'Create API Key' button in the org console while signed in via SSO? sometimes those keys are scoped to a service account or to a specific workspace. can you share the error body (redact tokens)?

Iris: body: ```{
  "error": {
    "type": "payment_required",
    "message": "Payment required",
    "code": 402
  }
}```

Jam: ok that's generic. check that the key's "workspace_id" matches the workspace you're selecting in the top-right. SSO users can accidentally create keys tied to a sandbox workspace. also check if the key is a service-account key vs a user key; SA keys sometimes inherit billing from a different org.

Iris: how do i check that quickly? the UI doesn't show workspace on the key list and the quickstart page only shows current workspace name in a tiny font. i thought the billing toast meant my workspace had no card and blocked me, but the card is on the billing page. confusing UX.

devex-bot: Created DX ticket DX-1503: "Quickstart: surface API key workspace scope and avoid ambiguous billing toast on first-call failures". Suggested quick wins: show workspace badge next to generated key, and if first-call returns 402 include safe billing_hint in response. Runbook: https://internal.docs/redwood/devex/keys-workspace-mapping

Omar: short-term: you can hit GET /v1/keys with your key to see metadata (workspace short_hash). example: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys``` will return a small object with workspace_hint. if workspace_short_hash doesn't match your selected workspace, generate a new key from the correct workspace.

Iris: ran that and it showed "workspace_hint": "ws_7f2..." which is different from my current workspace. regenerated a key from the correct workspace and first call is 200.

Jam: thanks for verifying. follow-up: we'll update the quickstart to print the key's workspace_hint on create and add a one-line QA check block in samples: ```// verify key workspace
const meta = await client.keys.get();
if(meta.workspace_hint !== expected) throw new Error('Key workspace mismatch');```

billing-ops: on the billing side i'll add a low-risk change: when returning 402 in the first-call flow include a non-sensitive billing_hint string and a CTA link to 'manage billing' for that workspace. we'll avoid exposing raw workspace ids.

Iris: resolved for me now. leaving this in case others hit it; small UX fixes would have saved time. thanks all! :raised_hands:
